requirements.outcome: Colored event fills lane bounds; lower name band turns black on selection. Media bounds exclude the reserved automation area.
Left drag moves events to matching Audio widths with transport snap settings and ghost/opaque preview.
White lower edge handles trim non-destructively and update audible source bounds.
White fade handles at both ends produce visible and audible fades.
White gain handle changes event amplitude with dB feedback and easy unity snap.
Event changes save/reopen and undo/redo without modifying source media.
Dark menu strip matches current dark panel background with white text.
Release startup avoids white/console flashing before the app frame.
Hold right button, hover cursor/scissors, release; shared toolbar tool follows.
Shared-grid/sample-aligned non-destructive cuts preserve source offsets and original fades.
Select two overlapping events and press X for actual linear fades, with undo/persistence.
Audio-event double-click opens lower-zone tabbed Sample Editor with waveform/overview/range and all-in-one editing structure.

Pitch & Time click explicitly starts cancellable Rust-owned F0/confidence analysis for current audio; valid results/editable state persist/reuse on save/reopen, and ordinary import/play/open does not analyze pitch.
Split/join/move/resize recognized note regions and repair tunable/unvoiced areas over original contour.
Independent pitch/time edits render audibly with source mapping, audition/bypass, history and stable real-time publication. Separate AudioWarp panel is excluded by user.
Evaluate optional neural detector/model runtime behind Rust interfaces independently of neural synthesis and preferred UI.
Both views show light-gray scissors guide on the same snapped/sample-aligned position used by cut commit.
Editor/overview share Project beat and engine seek, independent of source trim; ruler and playback stay aligned.
Mono source/track draws one waveform, stereo/stereo two, preserving track color and source metadata.
Compact toolbar/info/overview/sidebar/ruler structure follows supplied reference, with AudioWarp absent.
Arrow/scissors/pencil/zoom use available Windows-owned resources/installed artwork with native pointer feedback.
Independent persisted editor Snap/Grid/Quantize, default1/16, governs range/cut/ruler without changing Project grid.
Zoom/pan beyond source extent; middle pan and simultaneous ruler seek/zoom/held-edge scroll remain functional.
Event information fields are compact and mainly left aligned.
Scissors artwork anchors to exact snapped/sample-aligned cut guide rather than raw pointer.
Delete removes selected recorded audio events while retaining persistent pool membership and source files; Undo restores events.
Shift+Delete removes unshared paths/pool entries with byte-exact no-overwrite Undo/Redo and saved-project discard recovery.
An explicitly selected row is a separate deletion target; event removal cannot implicitly target the row on another Delete.
Pool survives deletion/save/reopen and allows retained media to be placed back into the project.
Native crosshair remains at raw pointer while scissors/guide stay at snapped cut hotspot.
Sample Editor ruler/waveform/overview mirror shared global loop/skip bounds, mode and enabled appearance.
Void primary drag box-selects audio events across lanes without seeking or dirtying Project.
Selected events move as one snapped, spacing-preserving, destination-validated group with one Undo/Redo step.
